input.question: Why do all the trains that transport coal do so without tarps or lids over the coal? Exposure to the elements
input.ground_truth: Because it's going to be stored in a giant pile outside when it gets to its destination, so it doesn't really matter. To expand on this: The vast majority of coal you see being transported is going to power stations where it will be pulverized into a fine powder and then launched into a super-hot fire by compressed air at the rate of about a thousand tons a day. So it isn't economical to protect such a huge amount of coal from the elements and it really doesn't matter if a little water goes into the fire along with it.

Question: Why do all the trains that transport coal do so without tarps or lids over the coal? Exposure to the elements

But with coal on a train, the coal is not something that gets ruined by rain or sun. In fact, sometimes the rain or snow even helps keep the coal wet, which can make it easier to move. Also, putting covers or tarps on all the coal cars would be really heavy and hard to manage. So, the trains just let the coal sit out in the open so it can get wet if it needs to, and it’s easier for the train to carry.

So, that’s why the coal trains don’t have covers!
